From 8ef14c2c41d962756d314f1d7dc972b0ea7a180f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Date: Tue, 6 Nov 2018 10:10:38 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] Revert "scripts/setlocalversion: git: Make -dirty check more
 robust"

This reverts commit 6147b1cf19651c7de297e69108b141fb30aa2349.

The reverted patch results in attempted write access to the source
repository, even if that repository is mounted read-only.

Output from "strace git status -uno --porcelain":

getcwd("/tmp/linux-test", 129)          = 16
open("/tmp/linux-test/.git/index.lock", O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_CLOEXEC, 0666) =
	-1 EROFS (Read-only file system)

While git appears to be able to handle this situation, a monitored
build environment (such as the one used for Chrome OS kernel builds)
may detect it and bail out with an access violation error. On top of
that, the attempted write access suggests that git _will_ write to the
file even if a build output directory is specified. Users may have the
reasonable expectation that the source repository remains untouched in
that situation.

Fixes: 6147b1cf19651 ("scripts/setlocalversion: git: Make -dirty check more robust"
Cc: Genki Sky <sky@genki.is>
Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Masahiro Yamada <yamada.masahiro@socionext.com>

diff --git a/scripts/setlocalversion b/scripts/setlocalversion
index 79f7dd57d571..71f39410691b 100755
--- a/scripts/setlocalversion
+++ b/scripts/setlocalversion
@@ -74,7 +74,7 @@ scm_version()
 		fi
 
 		# Check for uncommitted changes
-		if git status -uno --porcelain | grep -qv '^.. scripts/package'; then
+		if git diff-index --name-only HEAD | grep -qv "^scripts/package"; then
 			printf '%s' -dirty
 		fi
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `scripts/setlocalversion`**
   - The line that checks for uncommitted changes in the Git repository has been modified. 
   - The original line:
     ```bash
     if git status -uno --porcelain | grep -qv '^.. scripts/package'; then
     ```
   - Has been replaced with:
     ```bash
     if git diff-index --name-only HEAD | grep -qv "^scripts/package"; then
     ```
   - This change alters the method of checking for uncommitted changes, moving from using `git status` to `git diff-index`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `scripts/setlocalversion` is a direct response to issues caused by the previous implementation (commit 6147b1cf19651). The reverted change aimed to make the dirty check more robust but inadvertently led to write access attempts on a read-only repository, which could cause errors in monitored build environments. 
- By switching to `git diff-index`, the new implementation avoids the problematic write access while still checking for uncommitted changes, thus restoring the expected behavior of leaving the source repository untouched during builds.

Here is the commit message:
Revert "scripts/setlocalversion: git: Make -dirty check more
 robust"

This reverts commit 6147b1cf19651c7de297e69108b141fb30aa2349.

The reverted patch results in attempted write access to the source
repository, even if that repository is mounted read-only.

Output from "strace git status -uno --porcelain":

getcwd("/tmp/linux-test", 129)          = 16
open("/tmp/linux-test/.git/index.lock", O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_CLOEXEC, 0666) =
	-1 EROFS (Read-only file system)

While git appears to be able to handle this situation, a monitored
build environment (such as the one used for Chrome OS kernel builds)
may detect it and bail out with an access violation error. On top of
that, the attempted write access suggests that git _will_ write to the
file even if a build output directory is specified. Users may have the
reasonable expectation that the source repository remains untouched in
that situation.

Fixes: 6147b1cf19651 ("scripts/setlocalversion: git: Make -dirty check more robust"
Cc: Genki Sky <sky@genki.is>
Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Masahiro Yamada <yamada.masahiro@socionext.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the previous implementation of the dirty check in `scripts/setlocalversion`, which used `git status -uno --porcelain`. This command attempted to write to the Git index by creating a lock file, leading to write access attempts on a read-only file system. This behavior could trigger access violation errors in monitored build environments, where users expect the source repository to remain untouched.

Here is the patch:
 
 		# Check for uncommitted changes
-		if git status -uno --porcelain | grep -qv '^.. scripts/package'; then
+		if git diff-index --name-only HEAD | grep -qv "^scripts/package"; then
 			printf '%s' -dirty
 		fi

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```bash
git status -uno --porcelain
open("/tmp/linux-test/.git/index.lock", O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_CLOEXEC, 0666)
```
Reason:
The command `git status -uno --porcelain` attempts to create a lock file in the Git index, which requires write access. This leads to an error when executed on a read-only file system, causing access violation errors in monitored build environments where users expect the source repository to remain untouched.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```bash
git diff-index --name-only HEAD
```
Reason:
The command `git diff-index --name-only HEAD` checks for uncommitted changes without attempting to write to the Git index. This avoids the creation of a lock file, thus preventing write access attempts on a read-only file system and ensuring that the source repository remains untouched.
